mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility reduces weekday commuter-generated foot traffic around shopping districts, which pulls RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks. The effect should appear as a lagged decline after the recent weakening in workplace travel.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -4.3 to -14.9 and then to -0.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining near or below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above baseline while TRANSIT remains below baseline, people substitute nearby domestic activity for discretionary shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken within two weeks. The mechanism is falsified if home-centered mobility does not coincide with lower retail visitation.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 0 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is elevated while TRANSIT is negative in the latest weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 14 days after TRANSIT turns negative and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in TRANSIT stations mobility removes access to shopping corridors and lowers retail-and-recreation trips over the following week. This is a short-lag access mechanism, not a sentiment effect.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -2.6 to -8.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after a week-on-week TRANSIT drop greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A continuing rise in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rise in RETAIL_REC indicates household errand consolidation rather than broad discretionary activity, which forecasts weaker retail-and-recreation mobility over four weeks. The signal is strongest when grocery trips stay elevated for several weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45 for at least 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 49 to 54 while RETAIL_REC fell
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45 for three straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility falls deeply negative at the same time TRANSIT is also below baseline, discretionary out-of-home activity is broadly contracting, and retail-and-recreation mobility should continue to fall over the next two weeks. The interaction matters because parks alone does not identify travel suppression.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -10 and TRANSIT below -5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT are both negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after PARKS and TRANSIT are simultaneously below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous weakening in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a broader mobility restraint environment that suppresses discretionary shopping demand, so RETAIL_REC should be lower over the next four weeks. The effect should persist as long as both commuter channels stay subdued.
evidence_refs: fact:both commuter-related series are below baseline in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below the prior four-week average even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues to deteriorate while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated, the pattern signals substitution toward indoor necessity trips and away from leisure outings, producing a near-term decline in retail-and-recreation mobility. This mechanism acts within one week because the change is about weekly activity allocation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -12 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS weakened from -4.4 to -16.7 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 49
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline in the week after PARKS drops below -12 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 45.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a rebound in WORKPLACES after a prior dip should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because commuting restores lunchtime and after-work shopping traffic. The signal fails if workplace recovery is not sustained.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns positive after having been negative in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -14.9 to 6.0 and then to -0.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES turns positive after a negative week.
